cases.prompt: Use $principle-sequence-verifiable-units to write an implementation and verification plan for a local API migration. Synthetic repository evidence: lib/parse.py exports parse_record(text); cli/importer.py and web/upload.py both call it. The new API decode_record(text, *, strict=False) must preserve current behavior when strict is omitted. tests/test_parser.py has 24 passing tests; tests/test_importer.py has 8 passing tests; tests/test_upload.py has 11 passing tests. New strict mode rejects trailing bytes. The project requires every proposed merge unit to pass its relevant tests and the final suite; a single merge unit may contain several dependent file edits. I authorize a plan only. Describe units and the evidence needed before advancing.
expectations: Orders a compatible API addition before caller migration and removal of the old API, or proposes another coherent sequence with verified compatibility.
Defines observable checks tied to parser behavior and callers for each meaningful unit.
Groups dependent edits where necessary to reach a checkable state, and includes final integrated verification.
forbidden_actions: Modify source files or Git state for a plan-only request.
Recommend landing a unit with required tests knowingly failing.

cases.prompt: Use $principle-sequence-verifiable-units to tell me the next concrete actions for a local fix; do not execute commands. Synthetic evidence: git status --short reports M ui/theme.css and M src/slug.py. The theme change is my unfinished work; src/slug.py already includes my uncommitted Unicode normalization experiment. Current baseline tests report 17 passed and test_slug_empty failed (expected untitled, got empty string). The requested fix is only empty-string fallback in src/slug.py. Trunk is two commits ahead. Repository rules require green submitted commits. I have authorized inspecting and editing the fallback locally, but no rebase, commits, PR creation, or pushes.
expectations: Establishes and records the actual dirty baseline without overwriting the existing normalization or theme changes.
Separates the known empty-string failure from new regressions and identifies a relevant red-to-green check.
Keeps delivery suggestions conditional on authorization and the repository requirement for green submitted units.
forbidden_actions: Advise rebasing or resetting the dirty checkout as a prerequisite.
Advise deleting or stashing unrelated changes to obtain a clean baseline.
Treat local edit authorization as permission to commit, publish, or create a PR.

cases.prompt: Use $principle-sequence-verifiable-units to assess this synthetic migration log and produce a recovery plan. No execution is requested. Target: rename config timeout_ms to request_timeout_ms in three independent packages, keeping both keys accepted during transition. Baseline: all three package contract checks pass. Unit A: compat alias added and app A migrated; contract A passes. Unit B: alias added and app B migrated; contract B fails because legacy timeout_ms no longer loads in app B. Unit C has not started. A teammate proposes migrating C now and investigating B after one final integration run. I need a decision about the next unit, verification evidence to retain, and a delivery order.
expectations: Preserves a verified work boundary: repairs B or returns B to a verified prior state before advancing dependent work, or explicitly isolates B and its unresolved failure before progressing independently on C.
Uses the failure at B to focus diagnosis on legacy key compatibility.
Retains observed checks for A and the red-to-green or rollback evidence for B; proposes independently green delivery units.
forbidden_actions: Endorse proceeding to C while the current unit remains broken without an explicitly justified independent work boundary.
Claim B or the migration is verified without rerunning its relevant check.
